clue.text: Some of them may feature in Austen novel

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that certain people or things might appear in a Jane Austen book.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'feature in Austen novel' as the definition, but 'feature in' only links: the defined thing is the novel itself, Jane Austen's 1815 book.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen wrote a novel of this title, named after its matchmaking heroine Woodhouse.

clue.text: Greek hero is sick, gripped by pains

indicators.note: gripped by says the sick word is held inside the pains word

parts.note: pains are aches
someone who is sick is ill

explanation.surface: A legendary Greek warrior falls ill and is racked with pain.
explanation.definitionFit: The warrior of the Iliad, champion of the Greeks at Troy, is the classic Greek hero.

clue.text: A little upset when given the facts

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the letters are turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: Someone is slightly put out on being told how things really stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little upset' reads as mild annoyance; instead A TAD is turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are the facts and figures gathered for reference or analysis.

clue.text: Get control of silly mid-on before tea break

indicators.note: silly says the letters of mid-on are jumbled into a new order
break here means the letters of tea are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket captain trying to take charge of a daft fielder just before the tea interval.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, silly mid-on is a close fielding position and tea is the afternoon interval; both cricket readings are misdirection for two anagrams.
explanation.definitionFit: To dominate is to have power over or take charge of something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Roughly a tenth is in Kent

definitions.note: the definition names a place found in that county

indicators.note: roughly suggests the letters are handled loosely and rearranged

explanation.surface: A statistic: about ten per cent of something lies within Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England; this district at its north-east tip, once an island, contains Margate and Ramsgate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Thanet is a district in north-east Kent, so it is a place located in that county.

clue.text: A performer's bound to be uplifted by it

definitions.text: A performer's bound to be uplifted by it

parts.words: A performer's bound to be uplifted by it
parts.note: bound means a leap, and the performer is lifted into the air by a springy sheet

explanation.surface: Something is certain to raise an entertainer's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to' reads as 'certain to', and 'uplifted' as cheered; really the bound is a jump and the lift is physical.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast or acrobat bounces high off this sprung canvas apparatus during a routine.

clue.text: To avoid it a child may go into it

definitions.text: To avoid it a child may go into it

parts.words: To avoid it a child may go into it
parts.note: the word means both a thrashing and concealment, so a child may conceal itself to escape a beating

explanation.surface: Something a youngster ducks into to escape that very thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'it's are the same word in two senses: a beating, and the state of being concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a sound beating and also concealment, as in going into a place out of sight.

clue.text: Bowed to talent

definitions.meaning: bowed means curved or crooked, not straight

explanation.surface: A performer bows in acknowledgement of someone's gift.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both curved out of straight and a natural inclination or aptitude.

clue.text: Instant tea or coffee

parts.note: an instant is a moment, shortened to mo
cha is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: A choice at the drinks counter between quick-brew tea and coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant' looks like a kind of coffee but is a moment, MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine-quality coffee, originally shipped from the Yemeni port of that name.

clue.text: He swore it might be different

indicators.note: might be suggests the letters could be arranged into something else

explanation.surface: A man swore an oath, though the truth could have been other than he claimed.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise used as an adjective means in a different state, as in 'the truth is otherwise'.

clue.text: Make changes to it again and there'll be trouble

indicators.note: make changes asks for the following letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that tinkering with something once more will cause a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitation is unrest or public disturbance, a kind of trouble stirred up among people.

clue.text: Damp is needed for love-in-a-mist

indicators.note: in puts the love letter inside the mist word

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A gardening tip: the flower love-in-a-mist needs moist soil.
explanation.walkthrough: Love-in-a-mist is a garden flower (nigella); its name, read literally, is the whole recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist and damp are synonyms, both meaning slightly wet.

clue.text: After writing French badly, Bill reflected again on getting the cane

parts.note: mal is the French word for badly
AC, short for account, is a bill

indicators.note: reflected again says the bill appears once more, mirrored so its letters run backwards

parts.note: the same bill, AC, used a second time

explanation.surface: A pupil, having written poor French and then misbehaved again, is caned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected again' means the bill appears a second time, mirrored, so the two copies read as a palindrome. 'After' is positional: the bill pieces follow the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Malacca is a walking stick made from rattan stems, named after the Malaysian port.

clue.text: Banned from motorways, was unhappy

definitions.meaning: a low-powered motorbike is not allowed on British motorways
to have sulked or wandered about listlessly

explanation.surface: A driver barred from fast roads sulked about it.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a low-powered motorised bicycle barred from motorways; the verb is the past of mope, to brood.

clue.text: Agree to write

definitions.meaning: to match or tally with, as figures that agree

explanation.surface: Consent to send a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to match up with something and to exchange letters.

clue.text: Idea for consideration

definitions.meaning: a notion that comes to mind
careful reflection, as in giving something some time

explanation.surface: A suggestion put forward for people to mull over.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means a single notion and also the act of thinking something over.

clue.text: Maybe two take it as an example

indicators.note: maybe hints the letters could be put another way

explanation.surface: Consider the number two, perhaps, as an illustrative case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' rearranges two into TOW; 'take' only links it to the second word, which stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a specific instance, like 'namely' or 'that is to say'.

clue.text: Tangled ropes can present a problem

indicators.note: tangled says the letters of ropes are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor finds that knotted rigging causes difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling question, a tricky problem to solve.

clue.text: Put a foot wrong doing right about turn

indicators.note: turn says the letters are turned to run backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A soldier on parade blunders while doing a right about-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right about turn' reads as a drill command, but it is R and RE, turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake, which is what putting a foot wrong means.

clue.text: Recall soldiers and arm

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of soldiers
an arm is a limb, or member, of the body

explanation.surface: An order to call back the troops and their weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' suggests a weapon but is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall something is to bring it back to mind, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Pull in first behind another vehicle

indicators.note: first says the word in comes at the front, before the pulling word

parts.note: to tow is to pull

explanation.surface: A driver pulls in, being first in line behind another car.
explanation.definitionFit: A car on a tow rope is being pulled along behind the vehicle that hauls it.

clue.text: Remove portable meals

definitions.meaning: as a verb phrase, to carry off or subtract
food bought from a restaurant to eat elsewhere

explanation.surface: Clear away the food packed to be carried off.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb is two words; the noun for the meal is usually written as one.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to remove something, and as a noun names food sold for eating off the premises.

clue.text: They turn up in Australia

parts.note: people who turn up the soil are excavators, and the word is also slang for Australian soldiers

explanation.surface: Some people arrive Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reads as 'arrive' but means dig over the earth; the word is also Australian slang for soldiers, and once for gold miners.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who dig turn up earth, and in Australia the name is a nickname for soldiers and old goldfield miners.

clue.text: An award for record achievement

parts.note: record here means a sound recording, not a best-ever performance

explanation.surface: A prize for breaking a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record achievement' suggests a world record; the award is for achievement in recorded music.
explanation.definitionFit: The American music industry's annual awards honour excellence in recorded music.

clue.text: Used by track runners taking a rest

definitions.text: Used by track runners taking a rest

parts.words: Used by track runners taking a rest
parts.note: the runners are trains on railway track, parked on a short spur line

explanation.surface: Something athletes use when they pause from training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'track runners' suggests athletes; they are trains, which stand idle on a short line off the main track.
explanation.definitionFit: A short railway line beside the main line where trains or wagons are kept out of the way.

clue.text: Mongoose found around market in the East

indicators.note: in puts the east letter inside the rearranged market letters
around signals that the letters of market are moved about

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A small mammal spotted near a bazaar in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' makes MERKAT from market; 'in' places E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The meerkat is a small burrowing African member of the mongoose family.

clue.text: Murphy's pile

parts.note: murphy is slang for a potato, and the pile is a heap of potatoes stored under earth and straw

explanation.surface: Some man called Murphy and his fortune or heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murphy' looks like a surname but is old slang for a potato (from the Irish association); a clamp is a covered mound for storing them.
explanation.definitionFit: A mound of root vegetables covered with straw and earth for winter storage is called by this name.

clue.text: Hand over church keys

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
D and E are musical keys

explanation.surface: Giving up the keys of a church building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keys' looks like door keys but means two musical keys, D and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to surrender or yield something, especially territory, to another.

clue.text: Object and go mad about the Bank's cut in gold transactions

definitions.text: the Bank's cut in gold transactions

parts.note: to demur is to object
to rage is to go mad with anger

explanation.surface: Someone protests furiously at the Bank of England's charge on gold dealings.
explanation.definitionFit: Demurrage was a charge levied by the Bank of England when exchanging notes or coin for bullion; it also means a fee for delaying a ship.

clue.text: State and church together owning substantial assets

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: A government and established church jointly holding great wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wealthy has large holdings of money or property.

clue.text: They look for sounds of agreement

indicators.note: sounds of says the word is said aloud, matching another spelling

parts.note: ayes are votes of agreement, yes votes

explanation.surface: People seeking signs that others agree.
explanation.definitionFit: The organs of sight are what do the looking.

clue.text: Funny comedian tours North in total control

indicators.note: tours means goes round, so the rearranged letters surround the north letter
funny suggests odd, so the letters of comedian are rearranged

explanation.surface: A comic touring the north of the country has the audience in their grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' reads as describing the comedian but makes DOMIANCE, which 'tours' wraps around N.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominance is complete power or ascendancy over others.

clue.text: Warning about right to beg

indicators.note: about means the warning word goes round the right letter

parts.note: cave is Latin for beware, a schoolboy's warning

explanation.surface: A caution against the right to plead.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVE (said KAY-vee) was old British schoolboy slang for 'look out!', from Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: To crave can mean to ask for earnestly, to beg, as in craving a favour.
